overview:
Stax is a strategy consulting firm with an integrated expert network, purpose-built for private equity. Founded in 1994 by Rafi Musher in Boston, the firm has spent 30+ years specializing in commercial due diligence (CDD), value creation, and exit planning for PE investors. Unlike pure expert networks that provide expert calls as their primary service, Stax combines expert interviews with proprietary data analytics, field surveys, and consulting-grade deliverables to produce research-grade due diligence reports.

In September 2025, Stax was acquired by Grant Thornton Advisors, now operating as 'Grant Thornton Stax.' Prior to that, Blue Point Capital Partners (managing $1.5B+ in committed capital) had made a platform investment in Stax in October 2021. The combined Grant Thornton Stax practice services almost 70% of the U.S.-based Private Equity International 300.

Stax differentiates through speed and analytical depth. The firm's data science team builds machine learning models, conducts location analytics, and creates predictive frameworks — overlaying these on primary research from expert interviews and field surveys. In one notable engagement, the team collected direct feedback from 1,200+ dentists, surgeons, and competitors for a dental implants due diligence.

history.narrative:
Rafi Musher founded Stax in 1994, recognizing that PE firms needed strategy consulting with both significant analytical content and an action-oriented approach. The founding team came from large consulting firms and improved the generalist case-team model by adding specialist teams. Mark Bremer joined as President shortly after founding, instilling a focus on analytics and data-driven insights. The PE practice launched in 1996.

Stax grew steadily for over two decades before institutional capital accelerated its expansion. In October 2021, Blue Point Capital Partners made a platform investment when Stax had 200+ employees. In November 2022, Stax acquired AMR International, a London-based boutique strategy consultancy founded in 1991 with 30+ consultants and 500+ PE engagements, establishing Stax's European presence. In August 2025, Grant Thornton Advisors announced the acquisition of Stax from Blue Point, with the deal closing in September 2025.

servicesDetailed.name: Commercial Due Diligence
servicesDetailed.description: Stax's core offering. Comprehensive market analysis covering market dynamics, customer decision journeys, and competitive dynamics. Assesses target's right-to-win, defensibility of market position, and forward-looking growth opportunities. Supports both buy-side and sell-side due diligence with research-grade deliverables.

servicesDetailed.name: Expert Calls & Primary Research
servicesDetailed.description: Extensive interview programs with C-suite executives, industry experts, and customers. Includes field surveys (web-based) with customers, non-customers, and industry experts. Cold-call survey programs optimized for rapid PE deal timelines.

servicesDetailed.name: Value Creation & Growth Strategy
servicesDetailed.description: Post-deal performance enhancement identifying new markets, pricing opportunities, and operational efficiencies for PE-backed portfolio companies.

servicesDetailed.name: Exit Planning & Sell-Side Positioning
servicesDetailed.description: Data-backed growth narratives and strategic positioning to maximize valuation at exit.

servicesDetailed.name: Data Analytics & Data Science
servicesDetailed.description: Dedicated data science team building machine learning models, predictive analytics, location analytics for site selection, and hyper-custom analytical models. Integrates with primary research for data-augmented due diligence.

aiPlatform.narrative: Stax positions itself as 'tech-enabled' rather than offering a standalone technology platform. The firm's data science team deploys analytics tools, machine learning models, and predictive frameworks internally to enhance consulting engagements. Capabilities include data extraction, ingestion, cleaning, location analytics, predictive modeling, and market sizing models. Unlike pure expert networks, Stax's technology serves its consulting practice rather than being a client-facing product.
